{{family name hatnote|[[Zhang (surname)|Zhang]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Zhang Wenhao''' ({{zh|s=张文浩}}; born 1964), also known as '''Wen-Hao Zhang''', is a Chinese [[plant physiology|plant physiologist]] and nutritionist at the [[Institute of Botany, Chinese Academy of Sciences]].

==Career==
In 1991, Zhang and [[Stephen Tyerman]] studied [[sodium azide]] and concluded that by combining it with [[oxygen]] and using both on the [[hydraulic conductivity]] of the [[cell cortex]] will increase volumes of pressure relaxation.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.publish.csiro.au/paper/PP9910603|author1=WH Zhang|author2=SD Tyerman|title=Effect of Low O2 Concentration and Azide on Hydraulic Conductivity and Osmotic Volume of the Cortical Cells of Wheat Roots|journal=[[Functional Plant Biology]]|publisher=[[CSIRO Publishing]]|volume=18|issue=6|pages=603–613|year=1991|doi=10.1071/PP9910603|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 1999 he and Tyerman studied ''[[Triticum aestivum]]'' and how [[Mercury(II) chloride|mercuric chloride]] effects on hydraulic conductivity in that plant. During the experiment it was revealed that the inhibition of <math>Lp</math> and depolarization of <math>Vm</math> which is caused by <math>HgCl2</math> was similar to [[Hypoxia (medical)|hypoxia]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.plantphysiol.org/content/120/3/849.short|author1=Wen-Hao Zhang|author2=Stephen D. Tyerman|title=Inhibition of Water Channels by HgCl2 in Intact Wheat Root Cells|journal=[[Plant Physiology (journal)|Plant Physiology]]|publisher=[[American Society of Plant Physiologists]]|year=1999|volume=120|issue=3|pages=849–858|doi=10.1104/pp.120.3.849|pmc=59324|pmid=10398721}}</ref>

In 2001 he, Tyerman, and Peter Ryan have studied the same species again and how [[malic acid]] which is found on the [[Dental anatomy|tip or extreme end of a root]] is tolerant against [[aluminum]]. During the same study he also discovered that when Al<sub>3+</sub> is activated its permeability is higher than malate<sub>2−</sub> and contained anion channel antagonists such as niflumate and [[diphenylamine]]-2-[[carboxylic acid]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.plantphysiol.org/content/125/3/1459.short|author1=Wen-Hao Zhang|author2=Peter R. Ryan2|author3=Stephen D. Tyerman|title=Malate-Permeable Channels and Cation Channels Activated by Aluminum in the Apical Cells of Wheat Roots|journal=Plant Physiology|volume=125|issue=3|pages=1459–1472|doi=10.1104/pp.125.3.1459|pmc=65624|pmid=11244125|year=2001}}</ref>

In 2009 he along with Chinese colleagues studied [[nitric oxide]] in combination with [[nitrate reductase]] in both cold and freezing temperature on a plant species called ''[[Arabidopsis thaliana]]''. He discovered that when combining this with both <sub>nia1nia2</sub> and [[nitric oxide associated]] leaves the cold doesn't bother the plants as much, but it does bother its [[seed]]ings. He also discovered [[proline]] in wild plants and used nitrate reductase inhibitor with nitric oxide scavenger and donor to prove that there is positive correlation between them when it comes to freezing temperature.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.plantphysiol.org/content/151/2/755.short |author1=Min-Gui Zhao|author2=Lei Chen |author3=Li-Li Zhang |author4=Wen-Hao Zhang|title=Nitric Reductase-Dependent Nitric Oxide Production Is Involved in Cold Acclimation and Freezing Tolerance in Arabidopsis|journal=Plant Physiology|publisher=American Society of Plant Biologists|year=2009|volume=151|issue=2|pages=755–767|doi=10.1104/pp.109.140996 |pmid=19710235 |pmc=2754647}}</ref>

In June 2010 he along with American and Japanese colleagues had studied [[acid soil]]s and discovered that certain species of crop plants are resistant to [[soluble aluminium]]. The way how they do, he explained, is that the genes of ALMT and MATE families encode membrane proteins which produce [[anion]] [[Efflux (microbiology)|efflux]] called TaALMT1 across the [[cell membrane]].<ref>{{cite journal|author1=PR Ryan|author2=SD Tyerman|author3=T Sasaki |author4=Takuya Furuichi |author5=Yoko Yamamoto |author6=WH Zhang |author7=E Delhaize|url=http://jxb.oxfordjournals.org/content/62/1/9.short|title=The identification of aluminium-resistance genes provides opportunities for enhancing crop production on acid soils|journal=[[Journal of Experimental Botany]]|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|volume=62|issue=1|pages=9–20|year=2011|doi=10.1093/jxb/erq272|pmid=20847099 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
